Metronidazole and Estrogens (Conjugated Synthetic): Metronidazole can decrease the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but close monitoring is recommended. 2. Metronidazole and Ethanol: Metronidazole may increase the levels or effects of ethanol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 3. Metronidazole and Ethinylestradiol: Metronidazole can reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Close monitoring is recommended. 4. Metronidazole and Etoposide: Metronidazole may increase the levels or effects of etoposide by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Metronidazole and Fentanyl (Various Forms): Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, transmucosal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is necessary, patients should be closely monitored for respiratory depression and sedation, with fentanyl dose adjustments as needed. 6. Tetracycline and Fentanyl (Various Forms): Tetracycline may also increase the levels or effects of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, transmucosal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 7. Iron Supplements and Tetracycline: Iron supplements (e.g., ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate) can decrease the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 8. Metronidazole and Fluorouracil: Metronidazole increases the toxicity of fluorouracil by decreasing its elimination. Caution and close monitoring are required. 9. Metronidazole and Flibanserin: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 10. Metronidazole and Ibrutinib: Metronidazole increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. When co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, the ibrutinib dose should be reduced to 280 mg daily for B-cell malignancies or 420 mg daily for graft-versus-host disease. After discontinuation of the CYP3A4 inhibitor, the previous dose of ibrutinib should be resumed. 11. Metronidazole and Iloperidone: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Metronidazole and Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Metronidazole and Isoniazid: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of isoniazid by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Tetracycline and Ifosfamide: Tetracycline decreases the effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 15. Metronidazole and Irinotecan (Liposomal): Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of irinotecan (liposomal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 16. Tetracycline and Fondaparinux: Tetracycline increases the effects of fondaparinux through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but caution is advised. 17. Metronidazole and Guanfacine: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. For extended-release guanfacine, the dosage should be reduced to half of the recommended dose when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 18. Metronidazole and QTc-Prolonging Agents (e.g., Givinostat): Both metronidazole and givinostat can prolong the QTc interval. If co-administered, obtain ECGs at baseline, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 19. Metronidazole and Fexinidazole: Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 20. Metronidazole and Finerenone: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust the finerenone dosage as needed.
